value.scope:
The formalization gives two-fifths-power space simulation of a fixed deterministic machine with one writable tape and finitely many read-only input heads. Heads move at most one cell per step, initial contents are independent of the time bound, and contents and input symbols must be accessible in polylogarithmic space. Given a binary time cap $T\ge2$, the simulator returns the source's finite-control outcome and halting flag using $O(T^{2/5}(\log(T+2))^C)$ space.

A second simulator needs no time cap: on an input that halts at time $t$, it returns the halted outcome using $O((t+2)^{2/5}(\log(t+2))^C)$ space. Simulation time is unrestricted. General multitape simulation, hierarchy consequences, and bounded-space-halting results are outside these selected statements.

points.definitions_to_check: Single.sensor: initial writable-tape contents (tag none) and the symbols read by each of the `heads` read-only heads (tag some i) are an arbitrary function List X -> Option (Fin heads) -> Z -> A, constrained only through the `Access` hypothesis; input symbols share the tape alphabet A. This is the paper's 'uniform interface' (introduction.tex:33-38), not a restriction. The tape contents sensor x none do not depend on T by construction. ; Single.Access: the polylog-space accessor hypothesis is part of the statement (the theorem is conditional on it, per pair (x,T), as in the paper): a fixed uniform TM A, given x, the cap T, the tag, and the sign and magnitude of l in binary, outputs sensor x h l within p*(log2(T+2))^q work bits for every tag and every |l| <= T. In `unknown` it is required for every T >= 2. ; TM / TM.Within / Window.bits: simulator and accessor model is a multi-tape machine (finite Q, finitely many work tapes with finite alphabets) with endmarked read-only heads on the public word and on each binary argument tape; space = sum over work tapes of (window span including the origin) * bit-width of the alphabet; input and cap tapes are not charged; NO time bound (matches 'simulation time is unrestricted'); standard counted-cell convention. ; Single.move / Single.outcome: halted states are absorbing (state, tape symbol and head positions unchanged), and outcome x n = (state, halted flag) after exactly n steps, so it equals the 'finite-control and halting outcome by time n'. ; [Fintype X]: the public alphabet is finite. ; Cost.Log / Cost.exponent: Log T = Real.log (T+2) / Real.log 2 (binary log of T+2); exponent = 2/5 used as a real power; the log exponent e is a natural number and c a positive real, both existentially quantified before x and T (they may depend on M, A, p, q only), matching O~ with 'a fixed constant C'. ; Mark.see / Mark.walk: read-only inputs are endmarked (0 = left marker, 1..len = symbols, len+1 = right marker) and heads are confined to [0, len+1]; standard.
points.note: Lean `capped` and `unknown` are the two clauses of the paper's single main theorem (introduction.tex:64-79) with `Single` = the fixed one-writable-tape machine, `Access` = the polylog-space accessor condition, `outcome` = (finite-control state, halted flag) with absorbing halting states, `Within` = work-space bits with no time bound, and `c*T^(2/5)*(log2(T+2))^e` = O~(T^{2/5}); no step beyond unfolding these definitions is needed. The summary's remark 'improving the square-root exponent' is a comparison with the classical bound, not a separate formal claim.

statements.name: thm:main
statements.text:
\label{thm:main}
Fix a deterministic machine with one writable tape and head, a fixed
number of read-only input heads, unit movement and fixed origins for
all heads, cap-independent symbol functions, and a fixed accessor as above.
For every public input \(x\) and supplied binary cap \(T\ge2\) for which
the access condition
holds, its finite-control and halting outcome by time \(T\) can be
computed deterministically in \(\softO(T^{2/5})\) work-space bits,
excluding storage for the read-only input. Simulation time is
unrestricted, and the final writable tape need not be materialized.
If the access condition holds for \((x,T)\) at every \(T\ge2\), and
the machine halts on \(x\) after \(t\) steps without a supplied running
time, its outcome can be computed in
\(\softO((t+2)^{2/5})\) work-space bits.
